subject: EU data locale confirmation + PrivateLink connector pledge — Medisphere trial
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medisphere.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick confirmation: EU compute + Private VPC connector for Medisphere pilot

Hi Soojin,

We're running through the compliance checklist ahead of our pilot and need a concise confirmation for two items we'll present to our security team tomorrow morning:

1) EU-resident compute: for the Medisphere pilot, can you confirm that customer inference and ephemeral logs will be served from an Amsterdam (eu-west-1) region with no cross-border tokenization to US regions by default?

2) Private connectivity: we need a brief inventory of the Private VPC connector (Privatelink) options you support for EU — including per-region endpoint FQDNs, peering IP ranges, and whether KMS keys are partitioned per-customer. Example ask: "Can you provide the connector hostname, expected CIDR ranges, and whether HSM-backed keys can be scoped to Medisphere?"

Also: a pointer to any SIG/CAIQ artifacts that speak to network boundaries would be great. If you have a one-page summary we can attach to our SOC 2 intake that would be ideal.

Apologies for the short notice — can you confirm by EOD (PST)? If needed, we can slot a 30-minute tech sync Monday.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Security Operations
Medisphere Health

[Attachment: internal SOC2 checklist (referenced)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medisphere.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: EU compute + Private VPC connector for Medisphere pilot

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, followed by the evidence pointers and next steps.

Summary (short):
- EU compute: YES — pilot traffic and ephemeral inference compute will be routed to our eu-west-1 (Amsterdam) tenancy. Persisted telemetry is configurable but defaults to eu-west-1 for EU customers. We do not route inference payloads to US regions by default.
- Private connectivity: YES — we provide a PrivateLink-style private endpoint for EU with per-customer peering. Hostnames and ranges attached.
- KMS: per-customer key rings in the EU region are supported; we can provision HSM-backed keys on request (supporting BYOK workflows).

Attachments I'm including with this email:
- medisphere_evidence_manifest_v1.pdf (1 page summary + pointers to CAIQ/SIG artifacts)

Technical notes (longer):
- Connector: private endpoint is a regional FQDN (example: pl-eu.redwood-inference.com). Each customer receives a dedicated endpoint behind the regional peering fabric; endpoints terminate inside our eu-west-1 VPC boundary.
- Networking: expected peer CIDRs are 10.100.32.0/28 (control plane) and a customer-allocated /28 for data peering — actual ranges will be assigned during onboarding.
- KMS/Key separation: we maintain per-tenant key rings in the region; default key material is managed, HSM/BYOK supported with standard KMS workflows and audit logs exported to the customer's monitoring bucket on request.
- Data residency: inference inputs, outputs, and model contexts are ephemeral in-eu unless customer selects a cross-region durability policy.

Next steps:
1) I've attached a 1-page manifest (medisphere_evidence_manifest_v1.pdf) that references the CAIQ sections and our SIG inventory.
2) Grace will follow up with a connector inventory CSV (privatelink_inventory.csv) that lists the planned endpoint FQDNs and example CIDRs.
3) If Medisphere wants HSM-backed keys we can expedite a BYOK onboarding; Marcus can scope costs/sla.

If that covers what you need for the SOC 2 intake, say so and we'll mark the doc as final. Otherwise I'm happy to jump on the call Monday — feel free to propose a slot.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: medisphere_evidence_manifest_v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medisphere.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: connector inventory + CIDR and keystore topology (private)

Forwarding the connector inventory as promised — see CSV and a small topology PNG attached. A couple of clarifying bullets below.

On Fri, 12 Jun 2026 at 11:02 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary (short):
> - EU compute: YES — pilot traffic and ephemeral inference compute will be routed to our eu-west-1 (Amsterdam) tenancy.
> - Private connectivity: YES — we provide a PrivateLink-style private endpoint for EU with per-customer peering.
> - KMS: per-customer key rings in the EU region are supported; HSM-backed keys on request.

Inventory highlights (from engineering):
- Endpoint FQDNs (examples):
  - pl-eu-1.redwood-inference.com
  - pl-eu-2.redwood-inference.com
- Peering CIDRs (examples):
  - Control: 10.100.32.0/28 (used for orchestration/control signaling)
  - Data path: allocated per-customer (we typically assign a /28 per peering)
- TLS: mTLS between customer edge and our endpoint; client certs issued from our intermediate CA or you can present your cert if required.
- HSM/BYOK: supported via standard key wrap — we store key metadata in region and key material can be imported into an HSM-backed key ring in eu-west-1.
- Audit logs: VPC flow logs + access logs can be exported to your EU storage bucket (you control lifecycle) or sent to your SIEM via collector.

Attachments:
- privatelink_inventory.csv (attachment: CSV listing planned endpoints + example CIDRs)
- keystore_topology.png (attachment: small diagram of key separation and HSM flow)

Notes: if Medisphere's procurement needs a formal attestation doc for the SOC 2 packet we can provide a short signed addendum (one page) that confirms region residency for the pilot window.

Cheers,
Grace

[Attachment: privatelink_inventory.csv (CSV, 1 file)]
[Attachment: keystore_topology.png (PNG, 1 file)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medisphere.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EU data locale confirmation + PrivateLink connector pledge — Medisphere trial

Alex — quick operational commitments and a proposed timeline so you can close compliance gating: 

- Commitment: We will provision the dedicated eu-west-1 PrivateLink endpoint (single-tenant logical endpoint) scoped to Medisphere and ensure all inference compute for the pilot is pinned to eu-west-1.
- KMS: We will create a per-tenant key ring in eu-west-1; HSM-backed key import available within two business days of signed BYOK request.
- Audit package: we will attach the one-page attestation to your SOC 2 intake packet (signed PDF) and include the connector inventory CSV.
- SLA/fallback: if eu-west-1 capacity becomes constrained we will not fail over to US regions without explicit written agreement; default fallback is to scale within EU or throttle to maintain locality.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm acceptance of the one-page attestation (attached in manifest).
- Mon-Wed next week: Dedicated endpoint provisioning and cert exchange.
- Within 48 hours of provisioning: smoke test and export of flow logs to your EU bucket.

Please acknowledge and we'll open the provisioning ticket (PRJ-MDSP-1128). If you want the signed attestation into DocuSign we can send it there — I've attached the link below.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
